options: Access that, once granted, never expires or needs renewal
A type of multi-factor authentication challenge
Privileged access granted only for a limited, approved window when actually needed, then automatically revoked
A method for granting every user administrator rights by default
questions.explain: JIT access replaces standing privilege with a time-bound activation that ends automatically when the window closes.

questions.q: In Azure PIM, what does it mean for a user to be "eligible" for a role rather than "active" in it?
options: Eligible means they can activate the role when needed; active means the role is currently granted and usable
Active means the user has been denied the role entirely
Eligible and active mean exactly the same thing in PIM
Eligible means the role is permanently assigned with no activation step
questions.explain: A PIM-eligible user activates the role only when needed, for a time-bound window, rather than holding it continuously.

questions.q: What is an access review (certification campaign)?
options: An automated scan that deletes all user accounts older than one year
A tool for granting temporary privileged access instead of reviewing it
A one-time event performed only when a new employee is hired
A periodic process where managers or resource owners confirm whether existing access is still needed, revoking what isn't
questions.explain: Access reviews put the decision in the hands of the manager or resource owner, on a recurring schedule such as quarterly.

questions.q: Why is a manager or resource owner, rather than central IT, usually the right person to answer an access review question?
options: Central IT is not permitted to see access review data under any circumstances
Resource owners are required by law to approve all access requests
They're positioned to actually know whether a specific person still needs a specific access, unlike a central team reviewing a list in isolation
Managers always have more technical expertise than IT staff
questions.explain: The person closest to the actual job function can judge whether access is still needed; central IT usually can't make that call alone.

questions.q: What is access creep, and why does this lesson say it happens by default?
options: The slow, unintentional buildup of unneeded access, which accumulates through ordinary events like team changes and project wrap-ups unless something actively revokes it
A deliberate policy of granting excess access to improve productivity
An error that only occurs during initial account provisioning
A type of malware that specifically targets privileged accounts
questions.explain: Access creep results from small, reasonable-seeming decisions nobody reverses, which is exactly the gap access reviews close.
